body.statement: For fixed \(s\in[1,2]\), \(\tau_n=T_n\kappa_n^{1-1/s}\), and every strength sequence has a subsequence in exactly one component of \(\mathfrak R\). If \(s=1\), then \(T_n=\tau_n\), so the finite and divergent location-entropy faces remain distinct according to \(\lambda_n=\tau_n/\log(e/\kappa_n)\). If fixed \(s>1\) and \(\lambda_n\) remains bounded, then \(\tau_n\to0\); if fixed \(s>1\) and \(\tau_n\to\infty\), then \(\lambda_n\to\infty\). Thus cutoff recovery \(\mathsf{CR}(s,\kappa_\bullet)\) does not by itself imply shrinking effect intervals. The lower comparison at scale \(r_n\) is posed on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\), while attainment by the conservative finite-grid procedure is posed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\).
body.justification: The algebra separates global cutoff localization from the slope-induced indistinguishability that governs the causal effect label.
body.gap: Unknown-break papers classify location recovery, but the additional identity linking \(T_n\) and \(\tau_n\) is specific to the weak fuzzy-RD effect problem.
body.consumer: The partition tells an applied user which asymptotic statement is licensed by an estimated compliance strength and prevents use of a recovered-regime rate on a flat or critical face.
